class.copied_table: Copied. Paste it into a spreadsheet.
class.copy_failed: Copying didn’t work in this browser.
class.why_xc_ic: Extra credit +{n} on the in-class average
class.nothing_graded: Nothing graded for {name} in this term yet
class.nothing_graded_text: Mark a set of papers for it, or type in scores for work done before.
class.no_terms: Set up your terms to see them side by side.
class.read_failed: This class’s work couldn’t be read.
class.no_roster_text: Add the students’ names to see their grades, attendance and work here.
class.students_one_per_line: Students, one per line, in the order you want
class.roster_ph: Paste from a spreadsheet or your school’s system.
class.roster_note: Student ID and email columns are kept as each student’s details. Kept in this browser.
class.no_other_class: There is no other class yet.
class.notes_ph: Anything to remember about this student
class.bad_term: Give “{name}” a start and an end date, with the end after the start.
class.empty_t: When a type has nothing yet
class.fm_note: Feedback only: a tick, no score
class.leave_out_sub: See the class averages without them
class.move_down: Move down (further right in the gradebook)
class.move_up: Move up (further left in the gradebook)
class.not_a_score: That isn’t a score, so the cell was left as it was.

class.paste_bad.one: One was left as it was (not a score).
class.paste_bad.other: {n} were left as they were (not a score).

class.paste_left: Not on the roster, so left out: {names}. Type their scores in by hand.
class.paste_over: There were more lines than students; the extra ones were left out.
class.paste_ph: Paste a column of scores from a spreadsheet, in roster order, or names with scores beside them. Or type them in below.
class.retake_rule: When a student has more than one try
class.some_weight: Give at least one type some weight.
class.terms_hint: An assignment counts toward the term its due date falls in. You can move one to another term from its column. With no terms, everything is one year.
class.type_needs_name: Give every type a name, or remove the one with none.
class.type_twice: Two types are called “{name}”. Give each its own name.

class.type_used.one: One assignment is in this type. Give it another type first, or rename this one.
class.type_used.other: {n} assignments are in this type. Give them another type first, or rename this one.

class.types_hint: You can change any of them later from its column.
class.types_hint2: Inside each type, every assignment counts the same, whatever it’s out of: two assignments in a type worth 50% are 25% each.
class.types_title: What type is each of these?
class.types_w: Types, and what a grade is made of
class.untyped: {n} assignments have no type yet, so they don’t count toward a term grade.
class.untyped_one: “{name}” has no type yet, so it doesn’t count toward a term grade.
class.w_sum: These add up to {n}%. Each type counts in proportion, so the grade still works out of 100.
class.xc_each: Each point adds one percentage point to {where}. Leave a student blank for none. It doesn’t change any assignment’s score.
class.xc_each_ic: Each point adds one percentage point to {where}, which then counts by its weight. Leave a student blank for none.
class.charts_say: Every student and every assignment, shaded by score.
class.heat_say: Darker is higher. Press a heading to sort by it.
class.bands_say: How many students landed in each range.
class.compare_none: No class has a grade here yet.
class.compare_say: The average grade for each class over the same term, by the same weights.
class.u_grading: Change how the class is graded
class.add_levels_say: For a task you marked on paper or somewhere else.
class.crit_once: Criterion {k} has been assessed once this year.
class.crit_none: Criterion {k} has been assessed in no task this year.
class.crit_twice: Each criterion is usually assessed at least twice a year.
class.myp_say: Each task shows the level given for the criteria it assessed. The levels on the right are yours to set: press one to see all of a student’s evidence and choose the level that fits best. Levels are never averaged. The total and the grade appear once every criterion has a level.
class.fit_say: choose the level that fits best · {n} of {of} set
class.recent_not_set: Most recent is {last}. Not set yet.
class.below_lowest: This total is below the lowest boundary.
class.hint_say: The outlined number is only a hint from the most recent work. Nothing is set until you press, and pressing a set level again clears it.
class.tick_crit: Tick the criteria this task assessed.
class.level_whole: A level is a whole number from 0 to {n}.
class.pred_say: A predicted grade is your own judgment. The outlined number is what the percent earns on this class’s boundaries, as a hint. Nothing is set until you press, and pressing a set grade again clears it.
class.way_pts_say: Rubrics, points, a percent and a term average.
class.way_myp_say: Criteria marked 0 to 8, a best-fit level each term, a 1 to 7 grade.
class.way_dp_say: Marks for each component, turned into 1 to 7 by your boundaries.
class.now_myp: {name} is graded with IB MYP criteria
class.now_dp: {name} is graded as an IB DP class
class.now_pts: {name} is graded with points and percent
class.bounds_order: Each grade’s boundary has to be higher than the one below it.
class.one_counts: At least one component has to count.
class.criteria_say: Each is marked 0 to {n}. The names are yours to change.
class.bounds_myp: The lowest total of {n} for each grade.
class.bounds_published: These start as the published MYP boundaries. Change them if your school uses others.
class.bounds_scaled: No table is published for {n} criteria, so these are scaled from the four-criterion one. Check them against your school’s.
class.ib_holds: The app holds the names of the criteria and these boundaries, nothing else from the IB. Descriptors are yours to paste in.
class.bounds_dp: The lowest percent for each grade.
class.bounds_dp_say: These numbers are only somewhere to start, and are not any subject’s own. Type in the boundaries your subject and level use; they are different for each subject and can change with each exam session.
class.components_say: How much each type of work counts in this class.
class.components_note: A component is a type of work, such as Paper 1 or the internal assessment. Add or rename types in Term setup. These weights are for this class only: your other classes keep your usual ones.
class.way_pts_note: Each assignment has its own rubric or points, and the gradebook works out a percent and a term average.
class.bki_say: A gradebook downloaded from your school’s system or a spreadsheet: one row per student and one column per assignment. Assignments you already have are matched by name, and you check each match. Nothing is saved until you press Import, and nothing leaves this browser.
class.bki_kinds: CSV, TSV or Excel (.xlsx). In Google Sheets: File, Download, CSV.
class.bki_paste_ph: Or copy the cells in your spreadsheet, headings included, and paste them here.
class.bki_no_names: There’s no column of student names in that. Keep the names in one column (or first and last names in two), with a heading row above.
class.bki_no_scores: No column of scores was found. Scores need to be numbers, percents, “17/20”, or Missing and Excused.
class.bki_xlsx_bad: That Excel file couldn’t be read. Save it as CSV and choose that.
class.bki_xls_old: That is an old Excel file (.xls). Save it as .xlsx or CSV and choose that.
class.bki_build: This class has no students yet, so they become its roster.
class.bki_cats_say: Each one goes into one of your gradebook types. You can still change a single assignment below.
class.bki_new_type_say: A new type counts for nothing in the term grade until you give it a weight in Term setup.

class.bki_close.one: One name is close to an assignment you have.
class.bki_close.other: {n} names are close to an assignment you have.

class.bki_close_say: Say for each whether it is the same one, a new one, or to leave it out.
class.bki_close_tag: The names are close, not the same
class.bki_total: Looks like a total, so it’s left out
class.bki_out_of_now: Out of {n}, as it is now
class.bki_guess_say: Nothing in the file said what it’s out of, so this is a guess from the scores
class.bki_all_date: Date for every assignment without one
class.bki_no_date: An assignment with no date counts in no term until it has one. Set it here, or later from its column in the gradebook.
class.bki_rows_build: Each row becomes a student unless you leave it out.

class.bki_rows_un.one: This row doesn’t match anyone on your roster. Pick the student, or leave the row out. Nobody is added unless you choose that.
class.bki_rows_un.other: These rows don’t match anyone on your roster. Pick the student, or leave the row out. Nobody is added unless you choose that.

class.bki_add_taken: Add as a new student (the name is taken)
class.bki_all_match: Every row matches a student on your roster.
class.bki_absent: On your roster but not in the file, so nothing changes for them:

class.bki_fill_ids.one: Fill in 1 student ID where you have none.
class.bki_fill_ids.other: Fill in {n} student IDs where you have none.

class.bki_fill_mails.one: Fill in 1 email where you have none.
class.bki_fill_mails.other: Fill in {n} emails where you have none.

class.bki_differ.one: 1 student already has a different one, which stays.
class.bki_differ.other: {n} students already have a different one, which stays.

class.bki_clash.one: 1 score is already in the gradebook and differs from the file. Which should stay?
class.bki_clash.other: {n} scores are already in the gradebook and differ from the file. Which should stay?

class.bki_papers.one: 1 score already comes from a graded paper. It stays as it is; change it in the paper.
class.bki_papers.other: {n} scores already come from graded papers. Those stay as they are; change them in the paper.

class.bki_ask_first.one: Choose where one assignment goes first

class.mb_sub: One task’s scores in order, beside your school’s gradebook
class.mb_hint: Press a student once their score is in. Arrow keys work too.
class.gc_title: Bring a class over from Google Classroom
class.gc_say: Two downloads bring a class over. Both are read in this browser: nothing is sent anywhere, and there is no sign-in.
class.gc_1a: In Google Classroom, open the class, then any assignment’s Student work page.
class.gc_1b: Click the gear at the top right and choose Download all grades as CSV.
class.gc_kinds: A CSV, or the grades sheet saved as Excel (.xlsx).
class.gc_none: No students were found in that file. It needs one row per student, with their names in the first columns.
class.gc_roster_only: No columns of scores were found, so only the roster comes in.

class.gc_will_add.one: 1 student not on its roster yet will be added:
class.gc_will_add.other: {n} students not on its roster yet will be added:

class.gc_all_there: Everyone in the file is already on its roster.
class.gc_order: The roster is in the file’s order. You can reorder or rename it later on the class’s page.
class.gc_next: Next you see every assignment and score, and nothing is saved in the gradebook until you press Import there.
class.gc_make_check: Make the class and check the scores
class.gc_2a: In Google Drive, open the Classroom folder, then the class, then the assignment’s folder.
class.gc_2b: Download the folder. Drive makes a ZIP, and Google Docs come as Word files.
class.gc_2c: On the class’s Assignments tab, bring the ZIP in for that assignment.
class.gc_2_note: Files named “Student name - title” are put together under each student. A file a student uploaded under its own name opens as its own entry, for you to match.
class.gc_back: Scores can’t be sent back into Google Classroom from here. The Grades tab of an assignment lists every score to copy across.
class.ph_none: No scores in this class yet.
class.ph_out_of: Out of how many points? Leave it empty to type percents.
class.ph_tap_fb: Tap a student when their feedback is complete
class.ph_paper_say: Students with a scored paper show its score. Type one in for anyone without a paper.
class.att_saved: Each press is saved as you make it.
class.att_starts: Everyone starts as present. Press Late or Absent for anyone who isn’t, or “Everyone is here” if they all are.
class.att_keys: Absent starts as “reason unknown”; press “Absent, excused” once you know why. With a name in focus, P, L, A and E set it and move to the next student.
class.att_copied_day: Copied {day}. Paste it into a spreadsheet or your school’s system.

class.att_copied_n.one: Copied {n} day. Paste it into a spreadsheet.
class.att_copied_n.other: Copied {n} days. Paste it into a spreadsheet.

class.att_none_yet: No attendance saved for this class yet.
class.att_back_say: Click a date to open or change that day, or a name for that student’s page. “Here” counts everyone present or late.
class.att_unk_say: Open the day and press “Absent, excused” when you hear why.
class.seat_how: How is the room set up?

class.seat_how_say.one: Pick the closest one. There is a desk for the {n} student, and any desk can be moved or taken away afterwards.
class.seat_how_say.other: Pick the closest one. There is a desk for each of the {n} students, and any desk can be moved or taken away afterwards.

class.seat_pairs_say: Desks side by side in twos
class.seat_horseshoe_say: Desks around three sides, open to the front
class.seat_kept: Stays here when the class is shuffled
class.seat_desk_off: Desk {name}. Click to take it away
class.seat_desk_on: No desk. Click to put one here
class.seat_laid_out: The room is laid out again.

class.seat_no_desk.one: {n} student has no desk: “Arrange the room” in ⋯ adds desks.
class.seat_no_desk.other: {n} students have no desk: “Arrange the room” in ⋯ adds desks.

class.seat_arrange_say: Click a square to put a desk there or take it away.
class.seat_front_top: Front of the room at the top
class.seat_front_bottom: Front of the room at the bottom
class.seat_sel_say: click a desk to move them there.
class.seat_sel_say_drag: click a desk to move them there, or drag them.
class.seat_hint: Drag a student to a desk, or click the student and then the desk. Dropping one student on another swaps them. Drag someone here to take them off the chart.
class.pk_nobody: Nobody is marked as here. “Who’s here” puts students back.
class.pk_again_all: Everyone has had a turn. Starting again.
class.pk_who_say: Click anyone who is away today. They are left out of picks and groups until this page is closed.
class.mis_cut: The email was too long for a link, so its words are on the clipboard: paste them in.
class.mis_opened: Your mail app should open with the email ready to send.

class.mis_opened_bcc.one: Your mail app should open with one email to {n} student in Bcc.
class.mis_opened_bcc.other: Your mail app should open with one email to {n} students in Bcc.

class.mis_no_to: There is no email for {name} yet, so add who it goes to.

class.mis_left_out.one: {n} student with no email is left out.
class.mis_left_out.other: {n} students with no email are left out.

class.mis_copied.one: Copied {n} row. Paste it into a spreadsheet.
class.mis_copied.other: Copied {n} rows. Paste them into a spreadsheet.

class.mis_say: Each reminder opens in your own mail app, ready for you to read and send. Grading Studio sends nothing itself.
class.mis_none_year: Nobody owes any work this year.
class.mis_none_term: Nobody owes any work in this term.
class.mis_none_say: When you mark a paper Missing, on the marking screen or in the gradebook, it shows here.
class.mis_all_say: One email to all of them, each address hidden from the others (Bcc)
class.mis_words_say: Every reminder is written from these words. Your mail app adds your signature as usual.
class.mis_fills: Words that are filled in: {name} what the student is called · {class} the class · {list} the missing work, one on a line · {n} how many
class.mis_words_saved: Saved. Every reminder uses the new wording.
class.td_none: Nothing yet. Add what you need to do for this class.
class.td_add_ph: Add a to-do for this class
